text:
Pavel Buchnevich is a puzzle right now. The Blues hold 54% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, nearly six points better than without him, and yet he has two points in his last ten games and seven on the season.

Some of that is finishing (3 goals on 4.1 expected), but more of it is that the chances he's around simply haven't turned into much yet. His points per 60 sit well under the range we'd expect from him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, which is the worrying part: this isn't a single cold month on top of a great year.

The signature in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking is still there: 19% of his setups come from behind the net, more than twice a typical forward's rate. He's a 31-year-old with 506 career points coming in. Our range for the season is 33 to 54 points.
